content:
The U.S. government yesterday announced an update to its list of prohibited foreign-made products, adding "advanced robotic devices" to it. Today, a spokesperson for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) confirmed that the ban also applies to robot vacuum cleaners.

The robot vacuum ban affects Roomba, Roborock and other well-known brands, but you can continue to use your existing robot vacuum cleaner.

When the Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the United States, media attention focused on humanoid robots. But espionage doesn't necessarily require legs, and the FCC's robot ban is not limited to them either. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's director of media relations, confirmed to The Verge that the ban will cover robot vacuum cleaners. The ban will not be retroactive to your existing Roomba at home, and companies can continue to import and sell approved models. However, the government claims that future foreign robots will pose a national security risk, and even robot vacuum companies have suddenly been asked to commit to manufacturing in the United States.

The FCC believes that advanced robotic devices carry national security risks, and this also applies to some products we might consider harmless, such as robot vacuum cleaners, robotic lawn mowers, etc.

Unless a device has been explicitly approved, or is manufactured in the United States, it may not be sold locally.

The most upvoted comment was posted by CCATX

This cannot go on! Routers, electric vehicles, and now even robot vacuum cleaners are to be banned? It's absurd. I'm not naive and never view China as an ally beyond economic and political matters, but this approach is simply stupid. Overall, the best technology is made in China, whether it's smartphones, electric vehicles, or robot vacuum cleaners, and we have no one to blame but ourselves. Over the past four decades, we have repeatedly decided to move manufacturing overseas, while failing to invest in domestic education, manufacturing, and infrastructure.

This has nothing to do with national security. Any sane person would not believe that a robot vacuum cleaner poses a real threat to the United States. This is all just the Trump administration showing off and trying to circumvent more tariffs. If they truly want to bring manufacturing back to the United States, they should formulate a ten-year plan and actually start investing, because this is not something that can be achieved overnight. Banning widely popular technology products that make life more convenient and making life harder for Americans is absolutely not the right approach.

Since top brands like Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all Chinese companies, this ban is expected to hit the robot vacuum market particularly hard.

If you already own these products, you can still use them as normal for now; the FCC won't come to confiscate your robot vacuum cleaner.

However, depending on how the ban is ultimately enforced, the robot vacuum market could see dramatic changes in the short term. If this all sounds familiar, it's because a similar wireless router ban happened just a few months ago.

Will you continue to use your existing robot vacuum cleaner? Why? Let us know in the comments section.
